title: Reflexivity and Alternative Themes
summary: The same six invented extracts, two research questions and two theoretical lenses, giving four prepared accounts. Two pairings are coherent and two pull against themselves, and the mismatch is visible from outside.
learningObjectives: Explain how the research question and the theoretical lens together shape a thematic account.
Describe reflexivity as treating the analysts position as part of the analysis.
Judge whether a question and a lens are asking after the same kind of object.
Recognise that the same extract can be central under one reading and marginal under another.
Explain why several readings being possible is not the same as any reading being acceptable.
interactionTypes: pairing a research question with a theoretical lens
four prepared accounts, selected rather than generated
a map of where each of the six extracts sits under the current reading
a coherence rating that is visible from outside
privacy: Nothing is collected, stored or transmitted.
accessibilityNotes: Keyboard operable throughout, with both choices as labelled native selects. Where each extract sits is written out in words, at the margins or supporting or central, so nothing depends on a colour or a bar length. Every account states both what it illuminates and what it leaves less visible. Changes are announced through a polite live region. No timed content and no motion.
dataStatus: Fictional. The six extracts are invented for teaching and no participant, interview, institution or study is represented. Nothing is analysed by the page: four accounts were written in advance and selecting a pairing selects one of them.
simulationNotes: The two by two is chosen so that the coherent pairings sit on one diagonal and the strained ones on the other, which means changing either control alone moves from a coherent pairing to a strained one. Two questions and two lenses is a teaching simplification: there are many more of both, and a narrative, psychosocial or feminist reading would produce different accounts again. No software analyses qualitative data, and the page says so rather than implying otherwise.
readmeTopic: reflexivity, and why the account follows from the question and the lens
